overview.summary: Marketing managers plan how a product, service or organization is promoted, and lead the people who carry out the plans.
overview.problems: They help the right people discover, understand and choose what an organization offers.
overview.worksWith: Sales teams, designers, writers, product teams, agencies, analysts and customers.
overview.workplaces: Companies of every size, advertising and marketing agencies, non-profits and government bodies, in offices or remotely.

timeline.title: Review results
timeline.description: The manager checks how campaigns performed the day before: visits, sign-ups, sales and costs.
timeline.why: Numbers show what is working and what is not.

timeline.title: Planning campaigns
timeline.description: The manager decides the audience, message, channels, timing and budget for an upcoming campaign.
timeline.why: A clear plan avoids wasting money.

timeline.title: Working with the creative team
timeline.description: The manager briefs designers and writers, reviews drafts and gives feedback.
timeline.why: Clear briefs and feedback lead to better work.

timeline.title: Understanding customers
timeline.description: The manager reads customer feedback, surveys and market research to see what customers want.
timeline.why: Marketing works better when it matches real needs.

timeline.title: Budget and reporting
timeline.description: The manager tracks spending, reports results to senior managers and explains the choices that were made.
timeline.why: Organizations need to know that marketing money is well spent.

timeline.title: Launch days and fast changes
timeline.description: Product launches and events can mean long hours and quick changes of plan.
timeline.why: Timing is often fixed by the launch date.

responsibilities: Leading and coordinating teams and agencies
Protecting the organization's brand and reputation
Making sure promotion is honest and follows advertising rules
challenges: Results can be hard to measure and prove.
Budgets can be limited while expectations are high.
There is pressure to deliver growth.
Creativity has to be balanced with data and rules.
Brands compete hard for people's attention.
workEnvironment: Mostly office based, with a lot of meetings, teamwork and screen time. Roles range from in-house teams to agencies, where deadlines can be tighter. Some work involves events or travel.
rewards: Seeing a campaign reach and persuade people
A mix of creativity and data
tradeoffs: Pay and roles that vary by country and employer

activity.title: Plan a mini campaign for a school or community event
steps: Choose a real or imaginary event and write who you want to attend.
Write one clear message in a single sentence.
Choose two ways to reach your audience, such as a poster and a message to a class group, with permission.
Decide how you would measure success, such as how many people say they will come.
If it is something small, run the plan and note what worked.
activity.outcome: You practise defining an audience, writing a clear message and judging results.
activity.safety: Be honest in what you say, do not use other people's photos or names without permission, and share only in places where it is allowed.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
